findings.title: IssuedClaim signature has no defined message and no defined verification-key carrier; hash-only seat still REUSED
findings.claim: MLTP §4/§8(B) deliver a real RS256/Ed25519 signature check for every IssuedClaim, so a SHA-only verifier is caught with `sig-invalid`.
findings.stand_up: Take any IssuedClaim and ask the verifier contract two questions it must answer to compute `sig_verify(c.signature, d.delegated_key)`: (1) which bytes are signed? §4 defines `sig = SIGN(kid, context_string ‖ 0x1F ‖ canonical_bytes(target))` and enumerates context strings for release-root, delegation, witness-checkpoint and qual-state only — there is no context string and no `target` definition for an IssuedClaim (is it `payload`? payload+proof_material? the envelope minus `signature`? does it cover `claim_type`, `issued_at`, `qualification_state_ref`, `description`?). (2) which public key? The delegation statement carries only a fingerprint (trust-bootstrap §3); the TrustBundle §6 schema has no slot for the delegated public key (embedded_registries holds only witness/auditor keys); LocalTrustState §8.1 has none. A conformant implementation is therefore free to 'verify' by matching a fingerprint against key material it obtains from wherever and hashing whatever it chooses — exactly the KW-2 mutation — and nothing in the text rejects it. Mutation to redden: two independent verifiers (Q21 kernel diversity) pick different `target` coverage; a claim whose `issued_at`/`claim_type` was altered after signing is VERIFIED by one and `sig-invalid` by the other.
findings.spec_expected: MLTP §4:222-226 and §8.3:395 — signature verification REQUIRES RS256/Ed25519 over a payload the verifier rebuilds identically; KW-2 want = `sig-invalid`.
findings.spec_actual_reading: §4:240-242 defines the signature payload only for the four listed context types; the IssuedClaim `signature` block (§1.0:39-41) points to '§4 signature payload' which never names an IssuedClaim target. §8.3:393-395 verifies against `d.delegated_key`, but the delegation statement (trust-bootstrap:39-40) carries a fingerprint, and no bundle/LocalTrustState field carries the delegated public key (grep for jwk/public_key/pubkey in MLTP = 0). Meanwhile the CROSSWALK still declares the '6-line, SHA-256 only' PCL verifier as the REUSED seat (line 54) and PCL §6:146 still says 'only SHA-256' — the very claim v1.3 §4.1:178-179 calls wrong; the consistency audit C2 greps only the English phrase 'verified only with sha-256'. The spec states the intention but does not define the function; survival cannot be shown from the text.

findings.title: verify_bundle never binds claim inclusion proofs to release_root and never verifies the release-root signature — a pure SHA-256 acceptance path for claim content
findings.claim: 'One authority root (release_root)' plus RS256/Ed25519 signature means every accepted claim's content is bound to the signed, tlog-published release root; inclusion alone is never sufficient (KW-2 want).
findings.stand_up: Adversarial issuer (or anyone holding a delegated key with the right scope) builds a `legal-state` IssuedClaim whose `proof_material.pcl_inclusion` proves the payload under a Merkle root the attacker computed themselves, and signs it with the delegated key. Step A: `pcl_inclusion(c.payload, c.proof_material)` passes — PCL's `inclusion()` checks against `proof.merkle_root` (the proof's own root). Step C: `require bundle.release_anchor.release_root is THE authority root` compares nothing to the claim's root and verifies no signature over release_root. No step performs PCL's `root-mismatch` check or `RS256_verify` over the release root. Result: VERIFIED for a payload that is in no released, witnessed, logged root. Equivocation follows: consumer A gets `legal_state: IN`, consumer B gets `OUT` for the same (expression, valid_time, known_time), both signed by the delegated key, neither in the tlog, both VERIFIED — the transparency log and witnesses (steps E) constrain the release root, not the claims, so split-view detection does not reach IssuedClaims. This is literally the failure PCL §5 warns about ('inclusion alone … is not proof of authenticity').
findings.spec_expected: MLTP §5:273-283 'Η ΜΟΝΗ ρίζα αυθεντίας … κάθε TrustBundle δείχνει σε αυτήν'; §4:233 context `mltp2:release-root` implies the release root is signed and verified; PCL §5:126-133 `authentic()` requires `proof.merkle_root == corpus_proof.merkle_root` and `RS256_verify` over it; Q20:246-248 'ίδιο για κάθε καταναλωτή'.
findings.spec_actual_reading: In the executable contract §8.3:383-423 the only occurrence of release_root/merkle_root/root-mismatch is the tautological line 397; step A (385-387) calls inclusion only; no line verifies a signature over release_root or compares per-claim roots to it. The claim is bound solely by the delegated key's signature over an undefined message (A2-01). Q20's 'same artifact for every consumer' is not enforced by the verifier for claims.

findings.title: Scope is checked against `claim_type` but payload semantics follow `profile`; no binding check ⇒ out-of-scope analysis passes under an in-scope label
findings.claim: A delegated key with scope {release-signing} that signs a `jurisprudential-analysis` IssuedClaim is rejected with `delegation-scope-violation` (KW-10 want).
findings.stand_up: Holder of a delegated key whose scope is {legal-state} (or {release-signing}) issues an IssuedClaim with `claim_type: legal-state`, `profile: jurisprudential-analysis/1`, and a §2.6-shaped payload carrying `ratio`/`holding` without reviewer_adoption_act. Step B: `require c.claim_type IN d.scope` — passes (legal-state is in scope). Step I: `unadopted(analysis_claims)` — analysis claims are selected by claim_type (the only closed sum), so this claim is not treated as analysis. No error exists for claim_type/profile disagreement (taxonomy has `unknown-claim-type` only) and no step compares them. A consumer that 'acts only on the typed payload' per `profile` receives certified ratio/holding from a key never delegated for it, and A2-02 removes the release-root binding that might otherwise have caught the foreign payload.
findings.spec_expected: MLTP §8.2:376-378 'Το scope ελέγχεται έναντι του claim_type'; §1.0:34 'profile = το id του typed payload schema του claim_type' (i.e. profile should be a function of claim_type); KW-10 want = `delegation-scope-violation`.

Grep for any mismatch rule/error returns 0. The spec text does not close the substitution.

findings.title: Stale broader-scope delegation replay: `delegation_for(kid)` selection unspecified, `delegation_seq` self-declared, delegation-level revocation never consulted
findings.claim: The scope in force for a delegated key is the one the verifier checks; a narrowed/superseded delegation cannot be resurrected to widen scope.
findings.stand_up: Key K was delegated at seq=1 with scope {release-signing, jurisprudential-analysis}; later re-delegated at seq=2 with scope {release-signing} (or seq=1 revoked via a `trust-key-or-delegation-revocation` with `revoked_subject: delegation_seq=1`). Attacker (or careless issuer) includes both root-signed statements in `delegation_chain` and signs a `jurisprudential-analysis` claim with `signature.delegation_seq: 1`. Step B: `delegation_for(c.signature.kid, chain)` — undefined which statement it returns; nothing says 'highest seq wins' or 'reject if a higher seq exists'; the claim's own `delegation_seq` is the natural selector and it is attacker-chosen. Scope check passes against seq=1. Step G checks `revoked(c.signature.kid, r)` — by kid only — so a revocation whose subject is a delegation_seq is never matched. KW-10's expected `delegation-scope-violation` is not produced.
findings.spec_expected: trust-bootstrap §3:41 'Ανάκληση = νεότερο statement με μεγαλύτερο seq'; MLTP §2.8:161 revocation subject may be a `delegation_seq`; §8.2:376-378 scope enforced.
findings.spec_actual_reading: §8.3:393 selects a delegation by kid with no ordering rule; §1.0:40 lets the claim declare `delegation_seq`; §8.3:411 consults revocation by kid only; no text in MLTP mentions max/newest seq (grep = 0). The trust-bootstrap supersession rule is not carried into the verifier contract.

findings.title: Delegation validity window is checked against the delegation's own signing time, never against the claim's signing time — `delegation-expired` is unreachable
findings.claim: A claim signed after the delegation's `not_after` (or before `not_before`) is rejected (`delegation-expired`), i.e. delegation is time-bounded as trust-bootstrap §3 (≤1 year) and Q23 ('valid στο genTime του TSR') require.
findings.stand_up: Delegation D for key K: not_before=2026-01-01, not_after=2026-12-31, signed by root on 2026-01-01. On 2028-06-01 (delegation long expired, never explicitly revoked), K signs an IssuedClaim with an anchored issued_at of 2028-06-01. Step B evaluates `d.not_before <= d.signed_time <= d.not_after` — 2026-01-01 lies inside its own window — passes. Step B's claim loop checks scope and signature only. Step G checks revocation, not expiry. Result VERIFIED. The `delegation-expired` error in the taxonomy is never emitted by any step.
findings.spec_expected: trust-bootstrap §3:38-44 delegation carries not-before/not-after (≤1 έτος) and chain must be 'valid στο genTime του TSR'; Q23:283 same; MLTP §4:246 lists `delegation-expired`.
findings.spec_actual_reading: §8.3:391 compares the delegation window with `d.signed_time`, a property of the delegation itself; the claim's `t_sig` is only computed in step G (line 409) and never compared with any delegation window. The spec as written cannot produce `delegation-expired` for a claim.

findings.title: `issued_at` is a hash pointer to a TSR that is not in the bundle; the verifier reads `trusted_time` without verifying it ⇒ signature time is attacker-declared, defeating retroactive revocation offline
findings.claim: `issued_at` is a trusted, anchored signature time ('ΟΧΙ self-declared'); revocation with `invalid_from` is judged against it; the bundle is fully offline-resolvable.
findings.stand_up: Delegated key K is compromised; revocation published with reason key-compromise, invalid_from=T0. Attacker signs a fresh claim with K and writes `issued_at: {trusted_time: T0-1day, anchor: {tsr_sha256: <sha256 of any old TSR, or random>}}`. Offline verifier: TrustBundle §6 has no field carrying RFC-3161 token bytes (only `tsr_sha256` pointers), so it cannot check the TSR signature, its messageImprint (what was timestamped), or its genTime. Step G reads `t_sig = c.issued_at.trusted_time (anchored)` — '(anchored)' is a comment, not a check — and compares T0-1day < invalid_from ⇒ not revoked ⇒ VERIFIED. KW-6/KW-14's 'only signatures with independent RFC-3161 time before invalid_from survive' is unenforceable. The alternative anchor `tlog_leaf_index` is the issuer's own log (trust-bootstrap §1) and gives ordering, not time, unless a witnessed checkpoint is verified — and 'Witness 1 — GitHub' (trust-bootstrap §4) is a commit made by the issuer with no witness-key signature, so `witness_quorum(…, quorum=2)` has at most the TSAs, whose TSRs are absent.
findings.spec_expected: MLTP §1.0:49-53 issued_at = trusted anchor, not self-declared; §9:455-459 revocation judged against anchored t_sig; §6:301,313-317 'ΠΛΗΡΩΣ OFFLINE-RESOLVABLE … μέσα ή δεσμευμένα με inclusion proof'; §10:475 witnesses = GitHub + ≥2 TSAs.
findings.spec_actual_reading: Every TSR reference in MLTP is a `tsr_sha256` or prose (lines 43,50,87,269,275,362,427); the TrustBundle schema (293-308) contains zero TSR/timestamp-token fields; step G (409) consumes trusted_time without any verification step; no LocalTrustState field holds TSA trust anchors by name. GitHub 'witness' checkpoints have no signer key resolvable via `witness_key_registry` (trust-bootstrap:51-53 describes an issuer commit).

findings.title: With a trusted `now`, freshness is never computed: coverage `freshness` is never compared, an expired QualificationStateRecord degrades `level` but the result is still VERIFIED, and the receipt has no `level` field
findings.claim: Provider rule: without valid, fresh certification the answer is UNVERIFIED_FOR_MACHINE_RELIANCE/UNKNOWN; Q28: expired qualification ⇒ automatic downgrade; 'positive proof of freshness'.
findings.stand_up: Consumer has trusted_time.now = 2027-06-01 (evidence present). Bundle: coverage-and-freshness claim with freshness {as_of: 2026-01-01, max_staleness: 30d}; every QualificationStateRecord has expiry 2026-03-01. Step F: evidence not null ⇒ freshness_verdict is never assigned any value (the only assignment is UNKNOWN_FRESHNESS). Step H: `now > q.expiry` ⇒ q.level = none — a local variable, no error, no early return; `expired` from the taxonomy is never emitted. No step reads `max_staleness`/`as_of`. Step J: freshness_verdict ≠ UNKNOWN_FRESHNESS ⇒ `return VERIFIED`. The VerificationReceipt schema has `result` and `checks` but no qualification `level`, so the computed `none` is dropped. A provider following v1.3 §4.2 that consumes the receipt sees VERIFIED for a 17-month-stale, fully-expired bundle. Q28's negative witness ('βαθμίδα με ληγμένη φρεσκάδα ⇒ κοκκίνισμα') does not redden in the verifier contract.
findings.spec_expected: v1.3 §4.2:210-216 'Φρέσκια = εντός του freshness … αλλιώς UNKNOWN' and 'θετική απόδειξη φρεσκάδας'; MLTP §3:205-209 'Λήξη expiry ⇒ none'; Q28:330-337; §4:247 `expired` error exists.
findings.spec_actual_reading: §8.3:404-406 only sets UNKNOWN_FRESHNESS when evidence is null; 418 degrades a local `q.level`; 421-423 returns VERIFIED unconditionally otherwise; the pseudocode block contains zero references to coverage-and-freshness/max_staleness/as_of; receipt schema 331-338 has no level field. 'Positive proof of freshness' is implemented as 'absence of null'.

findings.title: QualificationStateRecord signer signature is never verified; `role` is self-declared; issuer check is a kid-denylist; auditor receipts may be unsigned — independence/quorum unenforced
findings.claim: Only independent auditors / auditor-quorum / provider-registry can confer a level; the release issuer can never qualify itself (KW-12 want) and evidence resolves to receipts of registered independent auditors.
findings.stand_up: Release issuer generates a second keypair K2 (not the release-authority kid, not in any registry). Writes a QualificationStateRecord {level: mission-qualified, signer: {role: 'auditor-quorum', kid: 'K2', sig: <anything>}, auditor_receipts: [two VerificationReceipts with verifier.id = names of real registered auditors and local_signature: null]}. Step H: `q.signer.role allowed_for(q.level)` — the role string is read from the record itself, passes; `q.signer.kid NOT release-authority kid` — K2 is not that kid, passes; no `sig_verify(q.signer.sig, …)` exists anywhere (the only two sig_verify calls are for delegations and issued claims); `evidence_resolves(…)` is undefined and the receipts' `local_signature` is schema-nullable, so unsigned receipts naming real auditors satisfy 'quorum'. Level mission-qualified stands.
findings.spec_expected: MLTP §3:190-209 signer role restrictions, 'release issuer ΔΕΝ μπορεί να υπογράψει για τον εαυτό του', evidence must resolve to receipts of independent auditors in the LocalTrustState registry; §4:220 QualificationStateRecord is a signed object under RS256/Ed25519 with context `mltp2:qual-state`.
findings.spec_actual_reading: §8.3:412-418 performs role/denylist/evidence checks with no signature verification and no requirement that q.signer.kid ∈ resolved `auditors`; §7:338 allows `local_signature: null` on receipts; `evidence_resolves`, `allowed_for`, `quorum_for` are undefined names. The self-qualification bar is a denylist on one kid, not an allowlist bound by signature.

findings.title: Revocation authority contradiction: a root-signed revocation IssuedClaim is rejected as `untrusted-key`, while a delegated revocation is scope-bound only by claim_type, not by `revoked_subject`
findings.claim: Revocations are issued by the root (key-lifecycle §2.5, trust-bootstrap §2.3) and published as `trust-key-or-delegation-revocation` IssuedClaims (MLTP §9); a compromised delegate cannot revoke keys it does not own.
findings.stand_up: (a) Root signs a key-compromise revocation for delegate K1 and it is published as an IssuedClaim (per §9:451-453). Step B: `delegation_for(root_kid, delegation_chain)` — the root has no delegation to itself ⇒ `untrusted-key` ⇒ the verifier rejects the very record meant to protect it; consumers relying on bundle-carried revocations never learn of the compromise. (b) If instead revocations are signed by a delegate D2 with scope ∋ trust-key-or-delegation-revocation, then an attacker holding D2 issues {revoked_subject: K1 (the honest release key), reason: key-compromise, invalid_from: 1970-01-01}. Step B: claim_type in scope ⇒ pass; nothing binds `revoked_subject` to subjects D2 may govern. Step G then returns `retroactively-revoked` for every honest claim ever signed by K1 — the verifier rejects what it must accept. `replacement_kid` is never consulted, so the attacker's key cannot be promoted, but total denial of the honest trust root is achieved with one signed object.
findings.spec_expected: key-lifecycle §2.5:55-56 revocation signed by root; trust-bootstrap §2.3:28-29 root signs ONLY delegations/revocations/ceremony; MLTP §9:451-453 revocation published as IssuedClaim in the tlog; §8.2:376-378 scope semantics.
findings.spec_actual_reading: §8.3:392-393 requires every IssuedClaim (including revocation claims) to resolve to a delegation by kid, which excludes the root; §2.8:161 `revoked_subject` is unconstrained; §8.2 scope is a set of claim_types, never a set of subjects. Two ACTIVE seats disagree on who may sign a revocation, and neither restricts what may be revoked.

findings.title: PCL §5 (ACTIVE SHARED TRUST FOUNDATION and the cited seat of MLTP §8) hard-pins `alg == "RS256"` and `thumbprint(public_key) == thumbprint(PINNED_KEY)` — algorithm/anchor confusion with MLTP; the consistency audit never reads PCL
findings.claim: Two ACTIVE specs never give opposite verdicts for the same signature (KW-16 principle); the crypto profile admits Ed25519 and a delegated release key.
findings.stand_up: Issuer completes the declared Ed25519 migration (MLTP §4:220, key-lifecycle §2.1) and signs the corpus-proof/release root with the delegated Ed25519 release key, embedding its public key. findings.title: 'Every IssuedClaim is proof-carrying' is false for 5 of 8 profiles — no `proof_material` is defined for source-authenticity, coverage-and-freshness, jurisprudential-analysis, correction/withdrawal, or revocation; step A is undefined for them
findings.claim: v1.3 §3: each IssuedClaim contains the proof object (De Bruijn); signature is in addition to proof, never instead.
findings.stand_up: Issue a `jurisprudential-analysis` (or `source-authenticity`, `coverage-and-freshness`, `legal-object-correction-or-withdrawal`, `trust-key-or-delegation-revocation`) IssuedClaim with `proof_material` absent or arbitrary. Step A runs `pcl_inclusion(c.payload, c.proof_material)` — for these profiles no proof_material shape is specified, so a verifier must either skip (silent acceptance, signature-only trust — exactly what §3 forbids) or reject every such claim (making 5 profiles unusable). Two kernel-diverse verifiers will choose differently (Q21 violated). For `source-authenticity` in particular, the payload holds only ids (`acquisition_receipt_id`, `authority_proof_ref`) — references, not the objects — so offline re-verification of provenance is impossible unless the referenced objects are bundle-carried, which §6 does not list.
findings.spec_expected: v1.3 §3:162-164 'κάθε IssuedClaim είναι proof-carrying … περιέχει το αντικείμενο απόδειξης'; MLTP §1.0:36-37 proof_material 'ανά profile'; §8.3:385-387 inclusion check for every claim.
findings.spec_actual_reading: §2 defines `proof_material` only at lines 99 (legal-state), 106 (temporal-projection), 125 (judgment-identity-and-text); the 8 profile headings (`### 2.1`…`### 2.8`) show 5 with none. The proof-carrying property is asserted, not delivered.

findings.title: tlog rollback: consistency against `last_accepted_tlog` accepts any older consistent prefix; no tree_size monotonicity ⇒ replay of a pre-revocation bundle passes split-view detection
findings.claim: Gossip/consistency (step E) makes equivocation and stale-state attacks detectable; revocations reach consumers 'μέσω consistency/gossip'.
findings.stand_up: Consumer's last_accepted_tlog = (N=1000, R1000). Attacker replays an archived bundle from tree size 800 (before a revocation leaf at index 850 and before the current revocation checkpoint). Consistency proof 800→1000 is valid (800 is a genuine prefix), so `consistency(bundle.transparency, lts.last_accepted_tlog)` succeeds; `split-view` is not raised because nothing requires `bundle.transparency.tree_size >= lts.last_accepted_tlog.tree_size`. Step G unions `lts.revocation_state` — protective only for consumers who already hold the revocation; a first-time consumer, or one whose revocation_state predates 850, sees none. A2-05/A2-07 ensure neither delegation expiry nor freshness stops the replay.
findings.spec_expected: trust-bootstrap §4:59-62 gossip rule; MLTP §8.3:401-403 split-view via consistency; §9:451-453 revocations visible via consistency/gossip; §6:304-305 'τρέχον revocation checkpoint'.
findings.spec_actual_reading: Both seats reject only a 'μη-συνεπές' (inconsistent) log; an older consistent tree is consistent by definition. No text requires monotone tree_size or that the bundle's revocation checkpoint be at least as new as the consumer's. Gossip therefore detects forks, not staleness.

findings.title: Crypto profile underspecified: no RSA modulus floor, no Ed25519 verification-variant pin, no fingerprint/key-encoding rule, no alg↔key-type binding — Q21 'identical result across independent verifiers' is unattainable on edge inputs
findings.claim: The 'real' crypto profile (MLTP §4) is complete enough that two independent kernels (Q21/Q22) yield identical VerificationReceipts and that `alg`/`kid` cannot be confused.
findings.stand_up: (1) Ed25519 signature crafted with a non-canonical S or small-order component: RFC 8032-strict, libsodium and ZIP215-style verifiers disagree; the two kernel-diverse verifiers emit VERIFIED vs `sig-invalid` for the same bundle — Q21(δ) 'δύο verifiers που διαφωνούν ⇒ αποτυχία' triggers by design, not by attack. (2) RS256 with a 1024-bit or e=3 key: nothing in MLTP/PCL/key-lifecycle sets a floor for keys carried in delegation statements (key-lifecycle says RSA-4096 'σήμερα', trust-bootstrap accepts RSA-3072; the verifier contract pins nothing). (3) 'fingerprint = sha256 του δημόσιου κλειδιού' (trust-bootstrap §2.2) does not say over which encoding (DER SPKI, PEM, JWK-thumbprint per PCL §4); two implementations compute different fingerprints for the same key ⇒ `delegation_for` resolves in one and yields `untrusted-key` in the other. (4) `alg` is chosen by the signer of the claim, the delegation statement carries no `alg`; the spec never states that alg must match the delegated key's type — within the closed set this is not directly exploitable (Ed25519 keys are 32 bytes), so it is a robustness gap rather than a break; `alg: none`/unknown survives via §4:237-238.
findings.spec_expected: Q21:261-262 'δεύτερη ανεξάρτητη υλοποίηση δίνει ταυτόσημο result'; MLTP §4:219-242 claims a 'ΠΡΑΓΜΑΤΙΚΟ' profile; PROOF-OBJECT §4 kernel diversity.
findings.spec_actual_reading: §4 names algorithms and context strings only; no parameters, encodings, or verification variants; trust-bootstrap:24-26 fingerprint definition is encoding-free; PCL:108 uses RFC 7638 thumbprints while trust-bootstrap uses raw sha256 — two fingerprint notions for one anchor.

summary: Both mandatory witnesses fall. KW-2 (A2-01/A2-02): the verifier contract states that RS256/Ed25519 is required, but never defines what bytes an IssuedClaim signature covers (context strings exist only for release-root, delegation, witness-checkpoint, qual-state), never defines where the delegated public key lives in an offline bundle (delegations carry a fingerprint; TrustBundle and LocalTrustState have no key slot), and — worse — verify_bundle checks per-claim Merkle inclusion against the proof's own root, never against release_root, and never verifies a signature over release_root; the crosswalk still REUSES the '6-line, SHA-256 only' PCL verifier as the seat. A pure hash path to VERIFIED exists for claim content, and transparency/gossip does not reach IssuedClaims, so per-consumer equivocation is undetectable. KW-10 (A2-03/A2-04): scope is enforced on `claim_type` while payload semantics follow the separate `profile` field with no binding rule, and a stale broader-scope delegation for the same kid can be replayed because `delegation_for` has no seq rule, the claim self-declares `delegation_seq`, and delegation-level revocations are never consulted. Beyond the declared witnesses, the delegation/time/freshness spine is not delivered as written: delegation validity windows are checked against themselves (A2-05, `delegation-expired` unreachable); `issued_at` is a hash pointer to an absent TSR and is read unverified, so the retroactive-revocation semantics of KW-6/KW-14 are attacker-controlled offline (A2-06); with a trusted `now` no freshness is ever computed, an expired qualification degrades a local variable but the receipt returns VERIFIED and cannot express level (A2-07). Qualification records are never signature-checked and auditor receipts may be unsigned (A2-08); root-signed revocations are rejected by step B while delegated revocations can retroactively revoke any kid (A2-09). Two stale-model contradictions survive in active/foundation text: v1.3 §4.1 item 2 says claims are signed by the pinned key (A2-10), and PCL §5 — the cited seat of MLTP §8 and outside the consistency audit's scope — hard-pins RS256 and pinned-key thumbprint equality (A2-11). 'Every IssuedClaim is proof-carrying' is false for 5 of 8 profiles (A2-12). Lower-severity gaps: tlog rollback via consistent older prefix (A2-13) and an under-specified parameter/encoding profile that defeats kernel-diversity identical results (A2-14). Survivals with cited closing text: unknown/none alg (MLTP §4:237-238) and Merkle domain separation/duplicate-last/path bound (PCL profile). No public→private boundary breach was constructed.
